analystPersona: an expert American football officiating analyst and former referee
observationHints: Look for contact before the ball arrives in pass plays, whether a blocker's hands are outside the defender's frame for holding, whether a defender initiated contact with the crown of their helmet or targeted the head/neck of a defenseless player, and whether a receiver secured the ball and survived contact with the ground to complete a catch.

rules.title: Defensive Pass Interference
rules.text: Defensive pass interference occurs when a defensive player contacts an eligible offensive receiver who has gone beyond the neutral zone, and their action obviously hinders the receiver's opportunity to catch the ball. It can only occur after a legal forward pass is thrown and before the pass is touched.

cues.description: Watch for contact occurring before the ball arrives. Contact that occurs after the ball is touched by any player is not pass interference.
Verify if the defender is looking back at the ball or playing solely through the receiver's back/body without looking.

rules.sanction: Spot foul (or 15 yards if NCAA), automatic first down.

rules.title: Pass Interference Exceptions
rules.text: Pass interference rules do not apply if: both players are making a simultaneous and bona fide attempt to reach, catch, or bat the pass. Contact that is unavoidable because both players are playing the ball is not pass interference.

exceptions.condition: Both players are looking back at the ball and actively attempting to catch it.
exceptions.outcome: Inherent or incidental contact is allowed; no interference foul.

rules.title: Offensive Pass Interference
rules.text: Offensive pass interference occurs when an offensive player contacts a defender beyond the neutral zone during a legal forward pass play and obviously hinders the defender's opportunity to make an interception or cover the receiver.

cues.description: Look for the receiver extending their arm fully to push away from the defender to create separation before catching the ball.
Check if an offensive player blocks a defender downfield before the pass is thrown or while it is in the air.

rules.title: Offensive Holding
rules.text: An offensive player may not use their hands, arms, or body to grasp, pull, hook, or encircle an opponent (other than the runner) to obstruct or block them. Hands must be kept inside the frame of the opponent's body during a legal block.

cues.description: Check if the blocker's hands are outside the defender's shoulders or frame. A jersey stretch/pull visible from behind or side is a strong holding indicator.
Look for the defender being pulled down to the turf as a result of the blocker grasping or hooking.

rules.title: Defensive Holding
rules.text: A defensive player may not use their hands or arms to hold, grasp, or pull an offensive player other than the runner. This is particularly applicable to holding receivers downfield or holding offensive linemen during a pass rush.

cues.description: Look for the defender grabbing the receiver's jersey or waist beyond 5 yards from the line of scrimmage, restricting their route.

rules.sanction: 10-yard penalty (or 5 yards + automatic first down depending on the league).

rules.title: Targeting (Crown of Helmet)
rules.text: No player shall initiate contact and write or make forcible contact against an opponent with the crown (top) of their helmet. This is an automatic safety violation designed to protect both the tackler and the tackled player.

cues.description: Check if the defender lowers their head, aligns the top of their helmet with the opponent, and launches.

rules.title: Targeting (Defenseless Player)
rules.text: No player shall initiate contact and make forcible contact to the head or neck area of a defenseless opponent. Defenseless opponents include: a player in the act of or just after throwing a pass, a receiver attempting to catch a pass, a runner on the ground, or a kicker.

cues.description: Verify if the player is in an unprotected position (e.g. tracking a pass in the air, legs in the air, or blindside).
Confirm if contact was made with the forearm, shoulder, or helmet directly to the opponent's head or neck area.

rules.title: Catch / Interception Requirements
rules.text: To complete a catch, an in-bounds player must: secure firm control of the ball with hands/arms, touch the ground in-bounds with both feet (NFL) or one foot (NCAA), and maintain control of the ball long enough to perform a common football move or maintain control when hitting the ground.

cues.description: Look for any movement or bobbling of the ball in the receiver's hands while touching the boundary lines or hitting the ground.
Verify that the player touches the ground in-bounds with the required foot/feet before going out of bounds.

rules.title: Incomplete Pass / Grounding
rules.text: A pass becomes incomplete when the receiver fails to secure control, or loses control of the ball during the process of hitting the ground. If the ball touches the ground before the receiver establishes full control, the pass is incomplete.

exceptions.condition: The ball touches the ground while the receiver is bobbling it, even if they later grab it firmly.

rules.title: Roughing the Passer
rules.text: No defensive player shall charge, tackle, or hit the passer after it is obvious the ball has been thrown. Special protection is given to the passer's legs (no low hits below the knee) and head/neck.

cues.description: Count the steps taken by the defender after the quarterback releases the ball. More than 1.5 steps usually indicates a late hit.
Check if the defender lunges at or hits the quarterback at or below the knees, or hits their helmet/face mask.

rules.sanction: 15 yards from previous spot + automatic first down.

rules.title: Roughing the Kicker
rules.text: It is a personal foul to run into or rough the kicker or holder of a kick. Roughing is defined as direct, forceful contact that endangers the kicker's safety.

exceptions.condition: A defender touches or blocks the kicked ball before making contact with the kicker.
exceptions.outcome: No foul for roughing or running into the kicker.

rules.title: Block in the Back
rules.text: An illegal block in the back is contact initiated from behind an opponent against their back, below the shoulders and above the waist. It does not apply against the runner.

cues.description: Watch if the blocker's path is strictly behind the defender, pushing their back or shoulder blades.

rules.title: Chop Block
rules.text: A chop block is a high-low combined block by two offensive players against a defensive player. One block is at or below the thigh, and the other is at the waist or above.

rules.title: False Start
rules.text: A false start occurs when any offensive player makes a sudden movement before the snap that simulates the start of the play. All offensive players must come to a complete stop and remain stationary for at least one full second before the snap.

cues.description: Look for offensive linemen twitching, flinching, or receivers moving abruptly forward before the ball is snapped.

rules.title: Offside (Defense)
rules.text: A defensive player is offside if they cross the neutral zone before the snap, make contact with an offensive player, or have an unobstructed path to the quarterback (unabated to the quarterback).
